indications.reason: Hepatitis B vaccination is routinely recommended for adults aged 19 to 59.
Adults aged 60 and older with known risk factors for hepatitis B should get the vaccine series. You reported a risk factor.
indications.section: Hepatitis B vaccination: Routine vaccination (age 60 years or older)

indications.reason: Adults aged 60 and older without known risk factors may get the hepatitis B series, and anyone this age who asks for it should get it. This app only checks some risk factors, so it's worth discussing.
indications.section: Hepatitis B vaccination: Routine vaccination (age 60 years or older)

series.note: This is the common 3-dose schedule (0, 1 and 6 months). Some hepatitis B vaccines use 2 or 4 doses. The product your provider uses decides the exact schedule.

contraindications.text: A severe allergic reaction (such as anaphylaxis) after a previous dose, or to a vaccine ingredient, including yeast.

precautions.text: A moderate or severe illness right now, with or without fever.

content.disease: Hepatitis B is a liver disease that can cause mild illness lasting a few weeks, or it can lead to a serious, lifelong illness.
content.why: The vaccine series prevents hepatitis B infection and the long-term liver disease it can cause.
content.who: Adults aged 19 to 59. Adults 60 and older with risk factors, and any adult 60 or older who wants it.
content.doses_text: Usually 3 doses over 6 months. Some vaccines use 2 doses one month apart.
content.catch_up: If you started a series and didn't finish, you don't need to restart. The remaining doses can be given.
common_reactions: Soreness where the shot was given
serious_reactions: People sometimes faint after medical procedures, including vaccination.
A severe allergic reaction is very rare.
